message.content:
Here’s a mix of well‑known and highly regarded sushi spots across Tokyo:

| Restaurant | Location | Highlights |
|------------|----------|-------------|
| **Sukiyabashi Jiro** | Ginza | Legendary Michelin‑starred spot (famous from *Jiro Dreams of Sushi*). Reservations required months in advance. |
| **Sushi Saito** | Minato | Three Michelin stars; intimate setting with a focus on seasonal ingredients. |
| **Sushi Yoshitake** | Chuo | Two Michelin stars; known for meticulous preparation and elegant plating. |
| **Sushi Mizutani** | Chuo | One Michelin star; offers a traditional Edomae style experience. |
| **Sushi Dai** | Tsukiji Outer Market | Popular for fresh fish and long lines; great value for the quality. |
| **Sushi Zanmai** | Multiple locations | Casual chain with a wide selection; open 24/7 at many sites. |
| **Sushi Kyubey** | Ginza | Classic Edomae sushi; renowned for its consistency and service. |
| **Sushi Iwa** | Shinjuku | Known for high-quality tuna and a relaxed atmosphere. |
| **Sushi Tsubaki** | Roppongi | Offers a modern twist on traditional sushi; excellent omakase options. |
| **Sushi Masuda** | Shibuya | Small, intimate setting; focuses on seasonal fish and precision. |

If you’re planning a visit, it’s wise to book reservations ahead—especially for the Michelin‑starred places—and consider the time of year, as availability can vary. Enjoy your sushi adventure!
